subject.title: [Proposal]: Add same-turn reread guard for first-class read tool to reduce token burn

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class `read` reread nudge by default, keep it behind `tools.loopDetection`, or treat the existing opt-in generic detector as sufficient?
rationale: The code already has an opt-in generic loop detector, but changing default read-tool behavior can affect legitimate debugging workflows and needs maintainer intent on thresholds and warning visibility.

options.title: Add opt-in read-aware detector first
options.body: Reuse the existing before-tool-call detector and add read/path-set heuristics under `tools.loopDetection` so maintainers can gather proof before any default-on change.

options.title: Enable a default warning-only read nudge
options.body: Solve the reported token-burn class for no-config users now, accepting the need for careful false-positive tests and visible recovery wording.

options.title: Keep existing generic detector only
options.body: Close or deprioritize this proposal if maintainers decide the current opt-in repeated-tool guard is enough for first-class reads.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in read-aware detector first
recommendation.body: Reuse the existing before-tool-call detector and add read/path-set heuristics under `tools.loopDetection` so maintainers can gather proof before any default-on change.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the original loop-detection feature and run-scoping behavior that this policy would likely extend.
